correctness.evidence: Independent sieve plus prime-indicator convolution reproduced all 21,000 unordered Goldbach counts sufficiently to match every published band sum, exact order/minimum gap, and the stated Hardy–Littlewood residual benchmarks.

originality.evidence: Durand (December 2025), Empirical Verification of the 2:1:1 Modular Law in Goldbach Partitions up to 300,000, publishes exact unordered Goldbach counts for every even target through 300000 and an open goldbach_counts.csv dataset (Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17042193). The record's entire [210000,252000) interval is a subset, and its exact band table is routine grouping of those prior values.

value.evidence: After prior-data coverage is removed, the remaining contribution is a standard singular-series normalization and finite-window regrouping. It does not yield a new theorem, algorithm, regime, or nontrivial reusable invariant beyond already-published pointwise counts.

checked_sources.title: Empirical Verification of the 2:1:1 Modular Law in Goldbach Partitions up to 300,000
checked_sources.author: Serge Durand
checked_sources.finding: Computes every unordered Goldbach count through target 300000, publishes the complete count dataset and code, and studies modular structure modulo 30. It strictly covers this record's target interval.

checked_sources.title: Goldbach's comet / Hardy–Littlewood singular-series literature
checked_sources.finding: The coarse modular banding and singular-series normalization are classical; the record's fine ordering is only an interval-specific aggregate.

limitations: Correctness is for the record's half-open interval [210000,252000), not the closed wording that appears elsewhere.
Residual statistics depend on the record's chosen asymptotic normalization.
